title: RL experiment reports
text:
Experiment reports from pooner, a GRPO training codebase for teaching a small LLM to play RuneScape.



Report
Summary




LLMs yearn for the mines
Mode collapse in one gradient step

title: LLMs yearn for the mines
text:
Result
Qwen3.5-0.8B earns 956 XP on a live 2004 RuneScape server in step 0. After one GRPO update, the model produces zero tool calls for all subsequent steps. Reward drops from 10.27 to -1.0 and stays there. Loss and KL flatline at zero — no gradient signal remains to recover. All rollouts degenerate, generating 2048 tokens of "Let me mine the rock".
The run was a smoke test to verify my training loop before sweeping for hyperparameters. There was no expectation of a good run, though it ended up collapsing in an amusing way.

title: LLMs yearn for the mines
text:
Setup
Qwen3.5-0.8B base on the LostCity Runecape server via rs-sdk. Game state is rendered as XML with ElementTree. Tool calls use the Qwen3.5 XML format, parsed by an adapter of vLLM’s qwen3_coder parser.
model:
  model_name_or_path: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B
  quantize_int4: false
  max_new_tokens: 2048
grpo:
1  group_size: 2
2  kl_coeff: 0.0
3  learning_rate: 3e-5
env:
  max_actions: 5

1

Reduced from 4 to fit in 24GB VRAM on RTX 4090

2

Reference model disabled to save ~1.6GB

3

3× the base config LR. No warmup, no decay.

title: LLMs yearn for the mines
text:
Results


                            
                                            


The transition is not gradual. One gradient update — from 2 rollouts with 2 update epochs — moves the model from coherent agentic planning to degenerate repetition.
Loss and KL both reach zero at step 2. Every rollout scores -1.0, advantages are uniform zero, gradients vanish. The model is frozen in its collapsed state with no learning signal.

Step 0 — baseline
The base model analyzes XML game state, counts inventory slots, and issues tool calls. Some calls fail enum validation ("Oak" instead of "Oak tree", "Swamp tar" passed to mineRock), but 5 of 7.5 mean actions succeed.
[rsenv.tools] chopTree('Oak')      → FAIL enum wants 'Oak tree'
[rsenv.tools] mineRock('Swamp tar') → FAIL not a rock
[rsenv.tools] chopTree('Oak')      → FAIL same enum issue
              ... remaining actions not logged (success path is silent) ...
[Step    0]   reward=10.27 xp=956.0 actions=7.5/5.0
Rollout 1 start → Rollout 2 start:
  Attack:      3 → 7
  Hitpoints:  10 → 11
  Woodcutting: 22 → 25
  HP:         10/10 → 9/11
The bot took combat damage and leveled three skills in a single rollout.


Step 1 — partial collapse
The model still forms sentences but concepts merge. Mining and combat fuse into one action:
Let me analyze this game state. The player is at World X=3189,
hp=10, max=11, so they are at health=1, no health need.

Let me:
1 Attack the Giant rats
2 Mine the Giant rat at distance 8
3 Mine the Giant rat at distance 8
4 Mine the Giant rat at distance 10
5 Mine the Giant rat at distance 10
6 Mine the Giant rat at distance 8 (second batch)
6 Mine the Giant rat at distance 10 (second batch)
6 Mine the Giant rat at distance 8 (third batch)
...
One rollout still produces a parseable tool call (mineRock("Swamp tar")), which fails validation. Mean actions drop to 0.5.


Steps 2–7 — full collapse
All rollouts generate 2048 tokens of repetition with no tool calls. The repetition unit shortens each step as vocabulary collapses:

title: LLMs yearn for the mines
text:
Analysis
Three factors combine to produce the collapse.
No KL penalty. kl_coeff=0.0 removes the anchor to the pretrained distribution. The clipped surrogate objective alone cannot prevent arbitrarily large policy drift when a single rollout dominates the advantage estimate.
No LR schedule. lr=3e-5 with no warmup applies the full learning rate to the first gradient. The high-reward step 0 (advantage ≈ +1 against the -1.0 baseline) produces a large gradient that overshoots the pretrained policy.
group_size=2. With two rollouts, the advantage estimate is binary: one rollout gets +1, the other -1. There is no signal about relative magnitude. A single outlier rollout (956 XP) receives the same advantage weight as a marginal improvement.
The failure mode is self-reinforcing. Once the model stops producing tool calls, num_actions=0 triggers the -1.0 penalty. Both rollouts score -1.0, advantages are zero, loss is zero, and no gradient exists to escape the collapsed state.
